I opened three issues, each written against a made-up repo `acme/xyz` like before: #52 for prompt templates, hiding tools and overrides, #53 for `AGENTS.md`, and #54 for skills. They link to each other. No repository files changed, so there was nothing to commit.

## Where pi-action is today on prompts, tools and overrides
This is what I found in the code, from pit v0.35.1 and pi-durable 1.5.2:

- **Prompt templates:** pi-action ignores them. pit ships `prompts/pit-reflect.md` through `pi.prompts`, but `loadExtensions` loads only `pi.durable`. So `@pi /pit-reflect` reaches the model as plain text.
- **Hiding or removing tools:** pi-action can't do this. In pi's command-line tool, pit hides `read`, `write`, `edit` and `bash` so the model sees only `typescript` (plus the `allowedTools` in `pit.json`). pi-action gives pi-durable only `{ model, cwd }`, so the model always gets `read, write, edit, bash, typescript`, and pit's `allowedTools` does nothing.
- **Overrides:** these partly work already, but nobody has documented or tested it. pi-durable applies the `wrapTool` and `wrapSection` of every installed extension, so a pi-durable extension can wrap `bash` or another extension's prompt section today. When two extensions have a tool with the same name, the last one silently wins.

## #52: Prompt templates, tool exclusion, and overrides from extensions
- **Two new inputs:**
  - `exclude_tools` removes a tool completely.
  - `model_tools_hidden` hides a tool from the model but keeps it callable through pit's `tools.*`.
  - Both accept `*` patterns and are applied on every run. A name that matches no tool gets a warning, and the run fails if the model would have no tools left.
- **Defaults set by an extension:** a pi-durable extension can't hide tools directly, but a wrap can. Setting a tool's `callers` to `["tools"]` stops offering it to the model while other tools can still call it. pit's durable entry could do this itself, following its `allowedTools`; that part would be a separate pit PR.
- **Templates:**
  - Load them from the extension packages' `pi.prompts`, from `.pi/prompts` (only with `trust_project`), and from `<agent_dir>/prompts`.
  - Expand `@pi /name args` the way pi does: `$ARGUMENTS`, `$1`, `${@:N}`, `${ARGUMENTS:-default}`. This applies to the task, `{{task}}` in `prompt_template`, follow-ups and the `prompt` input.
- **Overrides:** document and test the wraps, and log when one extension's tool replaces another with the same name.

## #53: Load `AGENTS.md` into the system prompt
- **Where:** a built-in pi-durable extension, `pi-action-context`, installed right after the coding tools. Its section, `<project_context>`, is formatted like pi's "Project Context" block and sits before pit's sections.
- **Which files:**
  - `<agent_dir>/AGENTS.md`, when `agent_dir` is set.
  - `AGENTS.md`, or else `CLAUDE.md`, in each directory from the workspace root down to `cwd`. It never looks above the checkout.
  - Nested files like `packages/api/AGENTS.md` are only listed by path, not loaded.
- **When:**
  - It reads the files once per run. Otherwise an edit to `AGENTS.md` during a run would change the system prompt and break the prompt cache.
  - New inputs `context_files` and `context_files_max_bytes`. I suggest defaulting `context_files` to `true`.
- **Security, needs your decision:** on a pull request, the author controls `AGENTS.md`. For pull requests from forks, the issue suggests reading it from the base branch or skipping it.

## #54: Load skills (SKILL.md) and list them in the system prompt
- **Where skills come from:**
  - The packages' `pi.skills`, or a `skills/` directory. Packages that contain only skills would also be installed, and there's an optional `skills` input for them.
  - `.pi/skills` and `.agents/skills`, only with `trust_project`.
  - `<agent_dir>/skills`.
- **Checking:** the `SKILL.md` header is checked against the Agent Skills rules (`name`, `description`, `disable-model-invocation`). When two skills share a name, the first one found wins and the rest get a warning.
- **In the prompt:** an `<available_skills>` section, built once per run, with each skill's name, description and full path. When `typescript` is the only tool the model sees, the instructions say to read skills with pit's `workspace.read` instead of the `read` tool.
- **Explicit use:** `@pi /skill:name args` puts the whole skill file into the message. It shares the task-rewriting code with prompt templates (#52).
